title: Nokcheongja Museum in Incheon: A Beginner's Guide to Korea's Only Celadon Pottery Museum
html:
If you've seen the elegant jade-green pottery called celadon (청자, cheongja) in a Korean museum and wondered how it was actually made centuries ago, there's a small, free museum in Incheon built just to answer that question. The Nokcheongja Museum (녹청자박물관) sits right next to the real kiln site where potters fired this pottery hundreds of years ago, and it's the only museum in Incheon dedicated entirely to celadon.

What Is the Nokcheongja Museum?

The museum opened in 2002 right next to the Gyeongseo-dong Nokcheongja Kiln Site (경서동 녹청자 요지), an official Historic Site that was designated back in 1970. "Nokcheongja" refers to an early, greenish style of celadon pottery that Korean potters were already making on this exact spot over a thousand years ago, before the more famous jade-green Goryeo celadon came later. The museum was built to protect and explain that kiln site, so you're not just looking at pottery in glass cases — you're standing where it was actually made.

What You'll See Inside

The museum has two small indoor halls. The History Exhibition Hall walks you through how celadon pottery was actually made — step by step, from shaping the clay to glazing and firing it in a kiln — which is an easy way to understand pottery-making even if you've never thought about it before. The Special Exhibition Hall next door shows the other side of the story: modern Korean ceramic artists using the same traditions to make brand-new designs.

Outside, there's also an outdoor exhibition area with around 200 donated pottery pieces, ranging from traditional shapes to much more modern-looking designs — it's worth the extra five minutes to walk around after you finish the two indoor halls.

Good to Know Before You Go

  • Address: 54 Doyoji-ro, Seo-gu, Incheon (경서동, Gyeongseo-dong)
  • Hours: 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:30)
  • Closed: Every Monday, the day after a public holiday, January 1, and the Lunar New Year & Chuseok holidays
  • Admission: Free
  • Parking: Available on-site
  • Phone: +82-32-563-4341 (Korean only — for English help, call the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline at +82-2-1330)

Because the "day after a public holiday" rule can shift the closed days around, it's worth a quick double-check before you go if your visit falls near a holiday.

Getting There

This museum sits in a quiet, residential part of western Incheon, well outside the usual Seoul tourist route — it's really a stop for travelers who already have extra time around Incheon, rather than a quick add-on to a Seoul day trip. There isn't one single well-known subway station right next to it, so the easiest way is to type the museum's name directly into Naver Map or Kakao Map — these are the apps Korean locals actually use to get around, and they're usually more accurate than Google Maps inside Korea — and get a live transit or taxi route from wherever you're starting. If you're driving or taking a taxi, you can also enter the coordinates 37.5583189054, 126.6562562073.

Since admission is free and this isn't a big, crowded spot, it works well as a slower, low-key stop if you're already exploring Incheon's Seo-gu area.

💬 Ever tried making pottery yourself, or have questions about visiting this museum? Drop them in the comments below — happy to help!
meta_description: Visit Korea's only celadon pottery museum in Incheon: free admission, two exhibit halls, and the ancient kiln site it was built to protect.
